body_text:
The Heine-Cantor Theorem. Every continuous function
$f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ on a closed bounded interval is
*uniformly continuous*.

*Significance*: Pointwise continuity allows $\delta$ to shrink
toward zero as $x$ approaches steep regions of the graph. On a
compact interval $[a, b]$, no such unbounded steepening can occur:
for any given $\epsilon > 0$, a single global $\delta > 0$
suffices for all points simultaneously. This uniform control is
the key technical requirement for proving the integrability of
continuous functions.
